title: प्रथमोनुवाकः
samhita: या ते॑ रुद्र शि॒वा त॒नूरघो॒रा-ऽपा॑पकाशिनी । तया॑ नस्त॒नुवा॒ शन्त॑मया॒ गिरि॑शन्ता॒भिचा॑कशीहि ॥
krama: या ते॒ । ते रु॑द्र । रु॒द्र शि॒वा । शि॒वा त॒नूः । त॒नूरघो॒रा । अ॒घो॒रा-ऽपा॑पकाशिनी । अ॒पा॑पकाशिनीति॑ अ॒पा॑प-काशिनी । तया॑ नः । नः॒ त॒नुवा॑ । त॒नुवा॒ शन्त॑मया । शन्त॑मया॒ गिरि॑शन्त । गिरि॑शन्ता॒भि । अ॒भि च॒क॒शी॒हि । च॒क॒शी॒हीति॑ चकाशिहि ॥

sayana.text: Indeed, Rudra has two bodies. As is heard later: "This Agni is indeed Rudra; he has these two bodies—one fierce and one auspicious." The injurious one is fierce; the graceful one is auspicious. O Rudra, that body of yours which is auspicious and performs grace upon us, is therefore non-terrible (aghora), not injurious. Its non-terribleness is clarified: 'Apapakahshini'—sin (papa) is of the form of injury or undesirable things; 'papakashini' would mean one who reveals such things; he is not like that, hence 'apapakahshini'. He who, staying on the mountain (giri) Kailasa, constantly extends (tanoti) happiness (sham) to living beings is 'Girishanta'. In that vocative case: O Girishanta, with that body which is 'shantamaya'—extremely conducive to happiness—look upon me (abhichakashihi), shed light toward me. The meaning is: having revealed such a body of yours, make me happy. (3)

bhatta_bhaskara.dhyana: "One should meditate on the Lord of Beings (Pashupati), the Controller, who has a smiling face, who is adorned with the crescent moon, who holds the Ganga, who is accompanied by the Daughter of the Mountain (Parvati), who has three eyes, and who is adorned with ashes and serpents." (3)
bhatta_bhaskara.text:
For 'Ya te rudra shiva tanuraghora', the Rishi is Kashyapa. The Deity is Shambhu. The Metre is Svarad-Anushtup. Some say Brihati, because it has more than three letters (or based on a specific count). The peaceful body is of two types: with weapons and without weapons. There, the first was described by the preceding mantra. The other body is described by this one. O Rudra, that body (tanuh) of yours which is auspicious (shiva), peaceful, and a cause of fearlessness. 'Tanuh' is a synonym for body, ending in a long 'u'. 'Aghora'—not cruel. To express the absence of the cause of two types of fear—one's own and that dependent on others—even after saying 'shiva' (auspicious), he says 'aghora' (non-terrible) again. He says the same: 'Apapakashini'—one who does not reveal sin or affliction (vyasana), because of the absence of weapons which are the causes of affliction. In both places, the un-augmented form is due to the prefix being an indeclinable. Or, it means one who does not reveal the sorrows which are the fruits of sin, because it is the cause of the destruction of sins for those who remember it. With that body (tanuva), with that most peaceful (shantamaya) form which is extremely conducive to happiness for those who remember it and which is of the nature of unsurpassed bliss. 'Nah'—upon us, 'abhichakashihi'—manifest again and again. The root 'kash' has a Vedic shortening. Or, 'achakashi' means 'looking'. It is a Vedic frequentative. This is the meaning: being such a one with a most peaceful body, look at us with a gaze of grace. O Girishanta—he who, having constantly manifested on the mountain Kailasa, extends happiness to beings. The suffix 'da' is added to the root 'tan' (to extend). Or, the mountain is the clouds; staying there, he extends happiness to beings in the form of rain (Parjanya). Or, staying in the mountain of speech, i.e., in the Veda, he extends happiness in the form of the meaning. Or, staying in the Pranava (Om), as the object of meditation, he extends the happiness characterized by the unsurpassed Bliss of Brahman. Some say...
...

10  

...meaning the suffix 'matup' expresses possession. He who resides with manifest happiness in places like Kailasa is 'Girishanta'.

Now for the Purashcharana of this mantra: having eaten sacrificial food (havishya) and chanting for three nights, one completes the Purashcharana. Now, with this, one should perform 'Go-shanti' (peace for cattle). Having made a fire-altar of one cubit in all directions in the middle of a cowshed, and having churned the fire, one should offer ten thousand sticks of Vaikangata and Apamarga wood, smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. Now, we will describe another peace-rite for cattle with this same mantra. Having consecrated pot-water with all perfumes by the Brahmins, and having chanted it a hundred thousand times, one should sprinkle the cows. Peace for the cows will ensue.

abhinava_shankara.dhyana: Meditation on Lord Maheshvara with resplendent Goddess.
abhinava_shankara.text:
That form of Yours, O Rudra, which is auspicious, which does not
        terrify, which illumines freedom from sin — with that peaceful form,
        O Girisha (Lord of the Mountain), shine forth upon us on all sides.

Having thus prayed in the second [mantra] for worldly happiness, and having
prayed in the third for the knowledge that is the cause of liberation (moksha)
— "ya te rudra" — O Rudra, that form (tanuh) of Yours which is well-known,
as is heard in the Shruti: "tasya ete tanuvau ghore 'nya shiva 'nya" (Of Him
these two forms exist — one terrible, the other auspicious); and in the
Mahabharata as well: "The two forms of that God are known to brahmin
seers of the divine: one terrible and one auspicious, and those again a
hundredfold" —

— That form (tanuh): of what nature is it? It is answered: It is aghora —
not terrifying by means of weapons without cause; aghora means not ghora
(not terrifying). Not only is it the absence of terror, but further it is shiva —
auspicious, a bestower of happiness. And not merely a giver of worldly
happiness; rather, it bestows the knowledge that is the means to liberation
(moksha), which is the supreme human goal (paramapurusharta) — this is
declared by: "apapakashini." By the word apapa, the knowledge that is opposed
to sin — that is, the knowledge of Brahman (brahman-jnana, the knowledge of
the supreme reality) — is indicated, as per the Shruti: "tad yathaisika-tulam
agnau protam praduyeta evam ha va asya sarve papmanah praduyante" (just as
a reed's tip thrust into fire is burned up, so too all sins of this person are
burned away); and as the Gita states: "the fire of knowledge burns all actions
to ashes." Apapa (freedom from sin) + kashini (illuminer) = one who illumines
freedom from sin, i.e., a giver of knowledge — such is the meaning. [This is
confirmed by] the Shruti: "atmabuddhi-prakasham" (the light of Self-knowledge).

Such being that form of Yours: with that shantamaya (utterly tranquil)
tanva (form), the form that is of the nature of unclouded bliss — abhichakashihi
(shine forth upon us, illuminate us on all sides) — illuminate us completely,
as beings shining on all sides with the non-dual identity of Brahman and the
Self. "May all of this be known when this one thing is known" — [as the
Shruti says.] The form abhichakashihi, being a yak-tug verb form (an intensive),
shows the intensification of the verbal action indicating the seeking of complete
illumination — the meaning being "bring us to a direct, unmediated
realization of Brahman." The phrase "shantamaya abhichakashihi" shows that
the Supreme Lord is of the nature of consciousness-bliss (chidananda).

But, one might think: "If you want liberation through mere salutation alone,
[without] the great efforts of hearing, reflection, and deep meditation
(shravana, manana, nididhyasana), [why use the term girisha?]" — so the
second mode of address is used, correcting this misunderstanding:

"Girisha" —

— "Girisha": He who dwells (shete) in speech (giri) that has the form of a
vow (pratijnya) and extends (tanoti) welfare (sham, liberation) to people is
Girisha (the Lord of the Mountain/of Speech). [The meaning is:] even without
the labors of shravana (hearing) and the rest, simply through the aspiration
for liberation that arises from salutation to the Lord and from the mere
recitation of the Shri Rudra — which consists of the Lord's divine names —
liberation is attained. [This is confirmed by] the Shruti: "etair hi va amrito
bhavati" (by these [names/mantras] alone one indeed becomes immortal). Such
is the purport of the second mode of address.

The seer of this mantra is of the Svara lineage; the meter is Trishtup-
Anushtup (a mixed meter); the deity is Shambhu. The dhyana-shloka is: "May
one meditate upon the Lord of all living beings, the auspicious one — smiling-
faced, wearing the crescent moon as an ornament, bearing the Ganga, with
the daughter of the mountain [Parvati] as companion, three-eyed, adorned
with ashes and serpents."

Perfection (purashcarana-siddhi) is attained by continuous recitation for three
nights without break, in a way that does not conflict with one's daily
obligatory duties. This mantra is especially efficacious for the expiation of
the sin of cow-slaughter and similar offenses.

Thus [ends] the third mantra.
abhinava_shankara.sanskrit:
श्रीरुद्रभाष्यम् ।                       ४९

शरैव्ये ब्रह्मसंशिता' इति श्रवणात्; यद्रा श्रृणोतेर्हिंसाकर्मेण:
शप्रलये शरु:, शरव: शरा:, तेभ्यो हिवा शरव्या श्रुधि:;
तया शरव्यया— उपलक्षणमेतत्— तेन धनुषा, तया इष्वा च
न: अस्मान्, मृडय मुखय। अस्य मन्त्रस्य आत्रेयकृर्षि:;
अनुष्टुप्छन्द:, शंभुर्देवता। 'ध्यायेद्देवं सस्मितं स्यन्दनस्थं देव्या
सार्थे तेजसा दीप्यमानम् । इष्टिवषासालंकृताभ्यां भुजाभ्यां
शूराकारं स्तूयमानं सुरौघै:' । द्वादशदिनानि नित्यकर्मांवि-
रोधेन निशिशिथिनांव्यतिरेककाछे निरन्तरजपात्पुरश्चरणसि-
द्धि:; तत: प्रयोगाहौं भवति। दुर्भिक्षराष्ट्रक्षोभादिपरिहार-
प्रधानोऽयं मन्त्र: ।।

              या ते रुद्र शिवा तनूर्घोरापापका-
              शिनी। तया नस्तनुवा शांतमया गिरि-
              शांताभिचाकशीहि ।।

एवं द्वितीयेन सांसारिकसुखमाशाह्म तृतीयेन मोक्षहेलु-
ज्ञानमाशास्ते— या ते रुद्रेति। हे रुद्र, ते तव, या तनू:
प्रसिद्धा, श्रूयते हि— 'तस्यैते तनुवौ घोरान्या शिवान्या'
इति; भारतेऽपि 'द्वे तनू तस्य देवस्य देवज्ञा ब्राह्मणा-
विदु: । घोरा चान्या शिवा चान्या ते चैव शतधा पुन:'
                         R. B. 4
